key_insight: A guided diffusion model can reconstruct physically realistic bubbly-flow velocity fields from phase-limited measurements, even across the strong statistical mismatch between liquid and bubble phases.
engineering_relevance: This offers a promising generative prior for filling in missing velocity data in multiphase experiments and for recovering otherwise inaccessible 3D flow information from sparse 2D observations.
method: Train on 2D velocity slices extracted from fully resolved 3D DNS of buoyancy-driven bubbly flows.
Generate reconstructions both unconditionally and conditioned on the surrounding liquid flow.
Use simple patching of adjacent slices to approximate 3D flow inside a bubble.
evidence_signal: The reconstructed bubble-phase fields reproduce key statistical features of the flow, and the slice-patching procedure yields a reasonable 3D reconstruction inside a bubble.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on DNS-derived 2D slices and simple patching, so robustness on noisy experimental data and more complex geometries remains to be verified.
paper_title: Gappy Reconstruction of Bubbly Flows by Guided Diffusion Models
